result:
The 50 Cent intro's low frame rate is emulator cost on the guest CPU, not the video's own pacing, and not the renderer. PR #385 is out of draft and the finding is posted on #382. One loose end: the perflog soak on master came back FAIL on 3 of 10 predicted legs, and the rerun meant to explain that couldn't run.

**Native rate: 30 fps.** I read the boot movies off the console over read-only FTP. They are Sofdec MPEG-1 files at 640×480, 29.97 or 30 fps, decoded in software by the game. The long one, `teaser.sfd`, has 2,910 pictures over 97 s, and none is a coded repeat frame.

**The player drops frames to keep up.** In the 10 fps runs it shows only the I and P frames and drops every B frame. That puts a frame on screen every 100 ms, exactly the 6-vblank flip interval the runs measured.

**Two runs on ref 6561442869** (both finished before I started; I read their logs):

| | 10 fps stretch | 30 fps stretch |
|---|---|---|
| renderer thread busy | 4% | 4.5% |
| guest CPU thread busy | 97% | 98% |
| slow-path guest stores per second | 2,505,844 | 4,034 |

**Cause, from reading the code:** the game decodes each frame with the CPU straight into a live colour render surface (VRAM `0x021A4F80`). hakuX watches bound surfaces for CPU access, so every store into it traps:
- The store takes the slow path and runs `surface_access_callback`, which takes the renderer's lock and walks the surface lists.
- It then calls `tlb_set_dirty`, which can never re-enable fast writes on a watched page because the entry carries `TLB_FORCE_SLOW`.
- Every trap after the first write in a frame does nothing useful.

**The fix is named, not made**, since I had no grant for `hw/`: in `vk/surface.c`, suspend a surface's watch after its first write when no download is owed, and re-arm it before the upload or the next draw. That costs about two TLB flushes per frame, against roughly 238,000 trapped stores per frame today. It carries a race, because re-arming is asynchronous: a write landing in the gap could leave at most one frame partly stale. There is also no per-trap timer, so I can only bound the gain; whether it reaches 30 fps is for the fix's A/B test. NOTES §2c has the design, and the Next section of NOTES has the must-move and must-not-move legs.

**Master soak** (`1790417278-fps382-2945668`, perflog build of 2dc2b5c49a):
- **The movie stretch ran at 16 fps instead of 10.5.** The prediction required a stretch at or below 12 fps, so that leg failed.
- **The pacing leg had no data.** `hakuX-pace` is missing from the Nova runner's log filter, even though master's `dispatcher.sh` names it.
- **One store-rate leg had no window to read**, because the ≤12 fps stretch no longer existed. Over the actual movie stretch the trap rate was unchanged at 2.66M/s.
- **The renderer is confirmed idle:** 57.1 of 58.6 ms per frame, GPU 0.2 ms.

No code on this path changed between the two refs, so device state (the earlier runs came late in an overnight batch) is the likely cause of the 10.5-vs-16 spread. It is unconfirmed: the rerun without perflog (`1790417886-fps382-3356323`) failed with "title not on device", because the ISO has disappeared from the Nova. Either way the intro runs at about half its native rate.

**Console access:** I read the movies over FTP from the console, the same read-only access the host's staging script uses, and only after checking that no staging batch was running.

`preflight.sh` passes and the PR's `Files:` line matches the diff. CI was green on earlier heads and is running on the final, docs-only head. The notes, prediction and scripts are all in `docs/lanes/fps382/`.

To close the open question, someone needs to put `56550042-50_Cent_Bulletproof.xiso.iso` back on the Nova so the rerun can separate device state from the perflog build.
